exam: 2023年12月 第2套 · 仔细阅读 P2
title: A multitasker is one who can perform two or more tasks effec…

sents.en: A multitasker is one who can perform two or more tasks effectively at the same time, which·apart from the obvious differences·is similar to what a computer does.
sents.cn: 所谓“多面手”，是指能同时高效完成两项或更多任务的人，这——除了显而易见的差异外——与计算机的工作方式相似。

sents.en: The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time.
sents.cn: 这个概念确实源自技术领域，在那里它用来指能够同时执行多个任务的操作系统。

sents.en: However, the question is: can a person really be a multitasker?
sents.cn: 然而问题是：人真的能成为多面手吗？

sents.en: For most scientists, the answer is no. So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience, our brains do not handle multitasking situations well.
sents.cn: 对大多数科学家而言，答案是不能。以至于神经系统科学的专家表示，我们的大脑并不擅长应对多任务情境。

sents.en: As soon as two tasks require our attention, productivity suffers.
sents.cn: 一旦两项任务都要求我们投入注意力，效率就会下降。

sents.en: What we call multitasking, therefore, is in reality the ability to move more or less quickly from one task to another.
sents.cn: 因此，我们所谓的“多任务”，实际上是从一项任务切换到另一项任务、且切换速度快慢不一的能力。

sents.en: This requires two essential conditions: that one of the tasks needs to be automatic, like walking or eating, and that they both need different mental processes.
sents.cn: 这需要两个必要条件：其中一项任务必须是自动化的，比如走路或吃饭；并且两项任务需要运用不同的心理过程。

sents.en: Answering the phone and writing at the same time, for example.
sents.cn: 例如，一边接电话一边写字。

sents.en: However, on the other side of the coin there are people who maintain that it is possible to be, or at least seem to be, multitasking.
sents.cn: 然而，另一方面，也有人坚持认为，人有可能做到、或至少看上去是在进行多任务处理。

sents.en: A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance.
sents.cn: 最近一项研究得出结论：无论人们是否真的在同时处理多项任务，只要他们把这一活动感知为多任务，就会对表现产生积极影响。

sents.en: The business perspective offers a different view: multitasking is understood as the ability to adapt to all types of environment within a company and effectively undertake different activities within a set time frame.
sents.cn: 商业视角提供了不同的看法：多任务被视为适应公司内各类环境、并在既定时间框架内有效开展不同活动的能力。

sents.en: Indeed, many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking to improve their productivity.
sents.cn: 事实上，许多公司都在寻找擅长多任务的人，以提升生产率。

sents.en: From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their working practices.
sents.cn: 从这一不同视角看，你不仅能成为多面手，这种能力还可以被传授：在崇尚灵活工作方式的柔性组织中，这更容易做到。

sents.en: The benefits of multitasking are clear.
sents.cn: 多任务处理的好处显而易见。

sents.en: Being quicker and more efficient increases our performance and the number of tasks completed.
sents.cn: 更快、更高效能提升我们的表现和完成任务的数量。

sents.en: But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes.
sents.cn: 但同时关注多件事意味着专注力下降，而这可能导致更多错误。
